limitations: The claim combines three propositions with different evidence requirements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Cycorp never succeeded commercially in a big way but has stayed in business for 40 years, which very few AI companies manage.

statement.excerpt: Cyc (and the parent company, Cycorp, that Lenat formed to incubate it) never exploded commercially – but hardly anybody ever gives it credit for the fact that it is still in business 40 years later; very very few AI companies have survived that long.

from_speaker: very very few AI companies have survived that long
our_interpretation: Read forty years as an approximate description of the Cyc project's continuity, including its later operation through Cycorp. Distinguish the project's age from the corporation's age.
The historical period runs from the project's inception in 1984, identified in the supplied screening context, through publication.
Commercial explosion means broad adoption or major commercial scale. Marcus states no revenue, valuation, or other financial metric.
The rarity comparison requires evidence about AI businesses old enough to have survived approximately forty years, with consistent treatment of projects, corporations, acquisitions, and successors.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes approximately forty years of project continuity and an operating commercial successor in 2023, limited commercial scale, and very few comparable surviving AI businesses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes a substantial interruption or closure, broad commercial success, or that comparable forty-year survival was common. A corporate founding date alone contradicts only a literal corporate-age reading.
